source_text.Q-1040: LOW, test-only, CI/test lane. test/letflow/engine/lua/executor_test.exs polling loops at ~L518 and ~L817 (Enum.reduce_while(1..20) with Process.sleep(10) = ~200 ms of observation) wait for a supervised Lua child while the script/call runs only timeout_ms 300; under host load the child can finish or not yet have started inside that window, so the assertion that a real in-flight child was observed can miss it. Fix: make the script deterministic instead of time-bound (script blocks on a message from the test, or the poll waits on a :started message plus a monotonic deadline well above the script's life; the script's duration is controlled by the test, not a sleep) so the window cannot close before the test looks; no global timing change. Mutation proof: a mutant that never spawns the child must still fail; stress: 100 consecutive runs under max_cases concurrency green (quote command and result). Acceptance: (1) both observation windows no longer depend on a fixed ~200 ms poll inside a 300 ms script; (2) mutant that never spawns the child still fails both tests; (3) 100 consecutive local runs under concurrency green, command and result quoted. Overlap: no open queue issue on executor_test; ISS-0456 (wasm_hang) is a different file. GH #2379.

result.summary: Root cause: tests at executor_test.exs ~L518 and ~L817 (nil max_heap_words, tagged lua_wallclock_race) observe the supervised child via 20x10ms polls of the GLOBAL Letflow.Engine.Lua.TaskSupervisor while the child lives only until Task.yield(300)+brutal_kill (lib/letflow/engine/lua/executor.ex:367-372). :started is sent before the spawn and the test polls on its own schedule, so a >300 ms test-process stall (child already killed) or late spawn gives children == []. Reproduced: with a 350 ms stall the existing poll returned [] (probe test outside repo, one mix invocation under the mutex, throwaway PG on 5499, removed). Also the global check can false-pass from other async tests children. 300 ms comes from REQ-155 (d932dbaec) as a short per-call timeout, not load-bearing. Fix is TEST-ONLY, no lib/ hook, no new tags (file asserts exactly 11 tagged tests): per test use timeout_ms ~30000, identify OWN child via the $callers pdict entry containing task.pid (probe-verified), poll with a monotonic ~5 s deadline, assert found, release by Process.exit(child, :kill) and assert {:error, "Letflow.Engine.Lua.Executor task crashed: :killed"} (probe-verified). Mutant: swap async_nolink at executor.ex:367 for Task.async -> both fixed tests miss the child and fail at deadline. Details in docs/issues/ISS-1040.yaml.
